Day 84 | Silt 25, Y.H. 813 (Fifthday) | the yard well, the Clay Yard and the bed under the Vail kiln-house roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | The bucket-round began before the light and a second man come downriver from Greybank, road-mud dried grey to the calf and the salt-and-hot-clay smell of the east road on him, told the yard of a counting room shut in the last war with the damper closed and the men inside dead of the breath when their heat went out with no way to feed it, a year two wars back and eighteen leagues east, and gave no name, so the yard took it as an old curiosity with a date, spoke of the war and of a room shut up being a room nobody entered on a slate, argued the thaw early against late and went home warm on the word without saying kiln or Vail; Sella told the fire it was the thaw and made nothing of it and did not touch the widow's mark, while the boy heard the breath and the damper where the yard heard a date, knew the anatomy of a room sealed against its own heat and filed the second telling on the same tray as the first without letting the two touch or joining either to any kiln; six hearings stayed six, three near-full answers stayed advanced and not paid, the word was not spoken, no collector came, the two lines stayed unswept, the payer of the coal stayed unnamed, the cold foot stayed the cold to one woman and weather to the yard, Dessa stayed forty mornings dead and uncollected, and at dusk Sella set him on the bed with one crust in the fold and the empty place unnamed, left the thread at his mouth frozen and unwiped, and the river's note came through the open door while the fire's missing breath came through the floor, the two kept apart as the count crossed into Silt 26 unspent.

Day 85 | Silt 26, Y.H. 813 (Sixthday) | the mud of the Clay Yard, the drying racks, the yard well and the bed under the Vail kiln-house roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | The mud had set into a brown skin over the ruts holding a boot's print and giving it back slowly, so Sella Vail told the broom to go around the clean dark line, the new finer grey called thaw and the space under the lowest rack where the broken birth-slates lay entered by nobody, and the yard counted its losses in loaves, glances and a space at the row's end nobody called a number while the boy, eighty-five days old, kept it exactly; over the bucket-round a woman said the shut-room story had a date in it and there was no third telling, so the boy kept the two tellings on their own tray joined to no kiln, one crust lay stiff in the fold with the empty place unnamed, Tarn's knife sat on its sill with six counted and his broom went over the collector's road without turning, the child's cold foot below the sill was still the cold to one woman and weather to the yard, and at dusk Sella set him on his bed with the fold put right and the thread at his mouth frozen as the count crossed into Silt 27 unspent.
Day 86 | Silt 27, Y.H. 813 (Seventhday) | the Clay Yard, the Vail wheel-shed, the back room (not entered) and the bed under the Vail roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | Before the light Tarn set the small bench knife on its sill and told the empty yard where it was, six years worn almost flat by his thumb and the seventh nearly gone and still held, the one entry in this house the house could not check, and said *Six counted. The next I don't count* to the kindling while going on holding the breath he had decided not to spend; he agreed so entirely with the early and the late thaw that no argument could find a foot and went on wanting the late because it puts off the paying, his broom went over the collector's road without turning and no collector came, Jorra Vail came through the wheel-shed door with grey slate dust worked past his bent little finger and named neither the men who had spoken low in the back room nor the room itself, spoke to the wheel before anyone, told a pot it would do, moved the damper ahead of Sella's unfinished sentence without looking toward the bed or the basket and kept *he's not Vail* sealed while a vessel gave its note past the door and neither man turned and the loan that can hear stayed uncalled, something having to give at the end of the seventh year that did not give here.
Day 87 | Silt 28, Y.H. 813 (Eighthday) | House Silt three doors down and the bed under the Vail kiln-house roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | Sella set the basket just inside the finger's-width-open door at the edge of the light and away from every place a slate might lie and opened no slate, and from the low angle the pewter tin above the empty bed kept its pale fold and thumb-bright rub while the grey wool below held only the hollow where the small pale river stone had lain and nobody said either was gone; Alda Reed came short with soap-and-milk gone cold under river silt, laid her birth-slates writing-down on the bench before she turned to the fold, pressed it a breath too long, crossed two fingers at the birth-flower before she knew it and covered the sign with the date of a woman more mornings dead than any living person keeps count of, said *Warm and breathing, that's all I've set down* which was exact and not true, touched the tin in her bodice without opening it and left her sixth narrow slate face-down with six pages unread, so that two private records in two materials stood apart in one room and were carried to no door as the count crossed into Silt 29 unspent.
Day 88 | Silt 29, Y.H. 813 (Ninthday) | the Fishstairs below the north bridge and the bed under the Vail roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | At the Fishstairs the steps came back four, four and a landing a hand's breadth out of line that a whole market walked over carefully without making a fall of it while the soft-cuffed clerk sat with his slate to his forearm for a measure nobody had called and his hand went to the slate before his eyes went to the stalls; Mira Silt worked the eels with pale slime dried on her sleeves and silt in the hollow of her neck, answered a question with her own answer and flicked eel-bones against her thumb while deciding whether to lie, put her thumb under her apron to the grey cord when a buyer named a figure and showed the second cord twisted twice beneath it, never carried to Nine Pots or lifted at a door with neither knot counted and the knot for the thin child upriver untouched, her board lying beside Orra's knot-string without touching it while Orra watched and got no answer, and at dusk Sella set the boy on his bed with one crust and the empty place unnamed and the fire's gap and the river's note in two places as the count crossed into Silt 30 unspent.
Day 89 | Silt 30, Y.H. 813 (Tenthday, Account-day) | the Cross, the moot-post's shade, the Fishstairs and the bed under the Vail roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | On Account-day and the last market of Silt Sella set the basket in the moot-post's finger's width of shade at the Cross with the cold iron at his cheek, and Berr Clay came up with the red wool cord folded under his coat and green glaze at one corner of his mouth, wiped his thumb twice before touching nothing, read one in twelve twice over the basket, passed a finger across the figure, said *The levy is called. It is not called by me* and *A number goes into a slate, not into a well* and went off toward High Kiln with the box locked and the true deduction inside believing he had done a kindness, while the number went from a fist to a mouth to a shoulder and arrived nowhere and the bell went four, four and a gap with nobody crossing himself; a woman with green at one corner of her mouth stood across the market and was filed in silence, the market walked carefully over the out-of-line landing at the Fishstairs with the clerk still set, and a small foundling in cast-offs turned his head toward a pot a half-beat after the boy's, rubbed the green sliver at his throat and could not say why, no loaf passing and no secret sold, as the last market closed and the count crossed into Seed unspent.
Day 90 | Seed 1, Y.H. 813 (Firstday) | the Clay Yard, the drying racks, the yard well and the bed under the Vail kiln-house roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | Seed opened on mud and the first work of the planting month was sweeping, not planting, as Sella gave the broom its instruction before anybody and went around the clean dark line, the new finer grey called thaw and the space under the lowest rack without sweeping any of the three; at the well she moved her lips along the loaf shelf, glanced at the clay jar and left the space at the row's end with no figure, telling the woman to ask the pot what a wet thing costs, while a man said the strips east of town would want hands by the morrow and a woman said the weather would have the last word and nobody put a figure to hands or strips, the boy ninety days old and three months setting the strips on a place of their own as a direction and not a number; Tarn's knife sat on its sill with six counted and the seventh held and his broom went over the collector's road without turning, Jorra was heard at the wheel and not seen, the carried fire kept four, four and a gap under blind ash with its payer unnamed for ninety days, one brown-edged crust lay stiff in the fold with the empty place beside it carried into Seed without a name and no third came, and at dusk Sella set him on his bed with the thread at his mouth frozen, the river's note through the finger's-width-open door and the fire's missing breath through the floor in two places, his hand going up an inch toward the water and down as the count went on unspent.
Day 91 | Seed 2, Y.H. 813 (Secondday) | the barley fields east of Low Kiln, the Clay Yard, the yard well and the bed under the Vail kiln-house roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | The direction carried for a month became worked ground as brooms went around the strips east of Low Kiln and seed went in from a fist in handfuls nobody counted aloud while a man said the strips would want hands and a woman said the weather would have the last word and neither put a figure to either, Berr Clay came down with his office cord folded under his coat, wiped his thumb twice before touching nothing, said a number goes into a slate, not a strip and that the levy was called but not by him, and went off toward High Kiln with his box locked and the true subtraction unspoken, at the well Sella Vail moved her lips along the loaf shelf, glanced at the clay jar and left the empty place at the row's end with no figure, telling the woman to ask the pot what a wet thing costs set down there and that the house had said it, while the boy, ninety-one days old, kept the count exactly against the house's loaves, glances and unnamed space, Tarn's knife sat on its sill with six counted and the seventh held, a vessel gave its note past the door and neither man turned, Jorra was heard at the wheel and not seen, the carried fire kept four, four and a gap under blind ash with its payer unnamed for ninety-one days, and at dusk Sella set him on his bed with one crust stiff in the fold, the empty place beside it still unnamed and no third, the river's note through the finger's-width-open door and the fire's gap through the floor in two places, his hand going up an inch toward the water and down as the count crossed into Seed 3 unspent.
Day 92 | Seed 3, Y.H. 813 (Thirdday) | the Vail wheel-shed and the back room (not entered), the Clay Yard and the bed under the Vail kiln-house roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | Men came in since first grey and spoke low in the back room and Jorra Vail gave them no name and did not say the room was cold, coming through the finger's-width-open wheel-shed door with fine grey slate dust worked into both forearms past the bend of his little finger, not bone-coloured slip, while the broken birth-slates stayed under the lowest rack entered by nobody, he spoke to the wheel before anyone (*It doesn't care whose hands. Day 94 | Seed 5, Y.H. 813 (Fifthday) | the barley fields east of Low Kiln, the Clay Yard, the yard well, the drying racks and the bed under the Vail kiln-house roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | The planting became worked ground as brooms went around the stone the flood had set in the strips and a woman's fist let seed out and came back with chaff in its creases while nobody put a figure to hands, strips or seed, Sella Vail gave the broom its instruction before anybody and never to the basket and told the woman at the well to ask the pot what a wet thing costs set down there because *the house has said it*, Tarn swept the collector's road over and over without once turning along it with six years counted and the seventh nearly gone and still held and said *Six counted. The next I don't count* to the kindling, and the boy, ninety-four days old, read the emptied fist as once he had read a chart closed with a neat line and a signature --- a clean reading worth nothing --- while his drool froze, his head went where it wanted with the small wet sound, cold arrived cheek, temple, wrist and his hand went up an inch toward the note of water and came down, at dusk the carried fire keeping four, four and a gap under blind ash and the back of a broken pot with its payer unnamed for ninety-four days and one brown-edged crust lying stiff in the fold with the empty place beside it still unnamed and no third.
Day 95 | Seed 6, Y.H. 813 (Sixthday) | the Vail kiln-house loaf shelf and clay jar, the Clay Yard and the bed under the Vail roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | A loaf's worth went off the shelf between dusk and light with no scrape, crumb, print or word so the row stood with two empty places where one used to stand --- the old space at the end nobody calls a number and a new palm's breadth of bare board with the next loaf settled a finger's breadth toward it --- and a neighbour's hand passed over the gap, opened for the half-beat it takes to find what is not there, closed on the loaf beyond and went on with her pot without a second look, while Sella moved her lips along the row, glanced at the clay jar, gave the instruction to the pot and the fire and never to the basket and said *the house* where another woman would say *I*, and the boy set the shelf's new gap and the empty place in the fold on two places that did not touch and wrote no cause across the space between them, having learned what three likenesses in a row will do to a man who wants an answer, wanting the number of his days said by somebody who would know what it counted and getting none, while Tarn's knife lay on its sill with six counted in a mark his thumb had worn almost flat and the seventh nearly gone and still held, a loaf carried out under a woman's arm went unentered and unnamed, and at dusk the fire missed its fifth breath with its payer unnamed for ninety-five days, the new grey lay unswept and was called the thaw and the fold kept one crust and one unnamed empty place in a room that did not touch the shelf's.
Day 96 | Seed 7, Y.H. 813 (Seventhday) | the back room off the Vail wheel-shed (not entered), the wheel-shed, the Clay Yard and the bed under the Vail roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | Men came in before first grey and spoke low in the finger's-width-open back room and were given no name, and Jorra Vail came through with fine grey slate dust worked into both forearms past the bend of his little finger, not bone-coloured slip, spoke to the wheel before anyone (*It doesn't care whose hands. It cares if they're steady*), told a pot *You'll do* and knew its full note before it left the wheel without saying so before a kiln-master from High Kiln who would call it early and make something of it, then put his bent finger into the damper ahead of Sella's unfinished sentence so the household straightened around his silence the way cloth straightens when a weight is lifted, while the broken birth-slates stayed under the lowest rack gone around as wide as a pail of hot water set where a child might knock it and entered by nobody and the boy read the iron as the bite that holds a vessel whole and can take a hand off a man with no Grathic word for both mercies and filed it as an object read perfectly and worth nothing, while Tarn's broom went over the collector's road without turning and he kept the unforged sentence from the frozen ford with the seventh year, a vessel gave its note past the door and his head did not turn and the boy did not call it a seventh hearing, *he's not Vail* stayed sealed and the promise of the foundling's name was neither given nor withdrawn, and at dusk one crust lay stiff in the fold with no third, the damper was cold under Jorra's bent finger and the room off the shed stood a finger's width open with no name given to the men.
Day 97 | Seed 8, Y.H. 813 (Eighthday) | the Fishstairs below the north bridge, House Silt three doors down and the bed under the Vail roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | Sella set the basket at the edge of the fish-trade shade where no slate lay and gave the instruction to the wool and the water and never to the basket, Mira Silt worked the eels with pale slime dried on her sleeves and silt in the hollow of her neck, answered whether the run would be thin with *Thin? Who's to say thin? It comes when it comes. Ask the river*, moved eel-bones against her thumb while deciding whether to lie and put one away when the deciding was done, and put her thumb under her apron to the grey cord when a buyer named a figure, shifting a creel to show a second cord twisted twice beneath it, never carried upriver to Nine Pots or lifted at a door with neither knot counted and the knot for the thin child upriver untouched, her board lying beside Orra Weir's knot-string without touching it while Orra watched and got no answer, the steps coming back four, four and a landing a hand's breadth out of line that a whole market walked over carefully without a fall and the soft-cuffed clerk still sitting at the landing with his slate to his forearm for a measure nobody called and his hand going to the slate before his eyes to the stalls, filed apart from Marra, the Drawing collector and the Court-table clerk with no sixth sighting of the neat dark hand, while three doors down in House Silt Alda Reed laid her birth-slates writing-down on the bench before turning to the fold, pressed it a breath too long, crossed two fingers at the birth-flower's red edge before she knew it, covered the sign with a date she had given a woman more mornings dead than any living person keeps count of, said *Warm and breathing, that's all I've set down* which was exact and not true, went on with dates after the question had stopped, touched the little tin in her bodice without opening it and turned her sixth narrow slate face-down toward a floorboard in a house the boy could not name so that the hidden record stood at six pages unread with no seventh written, while the pewter tin above the empty bed kept its pale fold and the grey wool below held only the hollow where the small pale stone had lain and the boy kept the two private records apart with the only instrument he had, which was attention, and bought nothing.
Day 98 | Seed 9, Y.H. 813 (Ninthday) | below the sill by the low houses, the edge of the Fishstairs market and the bed under the Vail roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | The water went out of the low houses and left a child with a foot that stayed dark inside three turns of wool while a woman wound it round and called it the cold and a neighbour at the tubs called the weather so the two facts went past each other and never met, and the boy read the extremity going before the core and the afterdrop waiting on the far side of a warming nobody would perform and had no word and no hand two paces long so the reading worked perfectly and was worth nothing, Sella shifting the basket out of the draught, saying *The house doesn't go down to a foot* and not going down though it was told of her in the yard that she once sat three nights with a child of her own who cooled while everybody was kind, while at the market's edge a small foundling in cast-off clothes worn like a uniform with silt dried pale in his wrists, a gap where a front tooth had been and a green sliver of lead-glaze on a string at his throat turned his head half a beat after the boy toward a pot set down, after the knuckle and after the note, then stopped, rubbed the sliver and could not say why, opened his mouth on the tail of a kiln-hand's unfinished sentence and let nothing out that a slate could take down, no new loaf passing and no slate being opened within reach of the basket while the warm loaf from Slate Row on Silt 16 went on gathering interest in an account the child could not read, and the boy filed the delay on a place of its own after the knock and not before it, not a hearing and not a seventh, and kept his own turning beside it without letting the two touch, the soft-cuffed clerk still set at the landing for a measure nobody called, and at dusk the cold foot lay on its own place and the half-beat on another with the damper's double bite filed as an object, six hearings six, one crust and its unnamed empty place and no third, and the fire's payer unnamed for ninety-eight days.
Day 99 | Seed 10, Y.H. 813 (Tenthday, Account-day) | the Cross (reading block and moot-post shade), a short turn at the Fishstairs landing and the bed under the Vail roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | Account-day turned out for the figure as for weather while eight pigs went over the wet reading block and a Sill assessor wrote them down before anybody could ask which eight he meant, his hand going to the slate before his eyes to the rail and then his mouth, an order the boy had seen in a midwife, at a well, behind a Court table, in a man who priced a basket and in a house that instructed a pot before a person, each instance on its own place and no cause joining them, and Berr Clay came up with the red wool cord of his office folded under his coat and green glaze at one corner of his mouth, wiped his thumb twice before touching nothing, read *one in twelve, as the notice says* twice over the basket, passed a finger over the figure, called the levy and said *It is not called by me* and *A number goes into a slate, not into a strip; if the house wants it again, there'll be a slate at the watch*, and went off toward High Kiln with the box locked and the true subtraction inside believing he had done a kindness, so that the number for the planting went from a fist to a mouth to a shoulder and arrived nowhere and a figure read aloud was not the figure paid, the bell going four, four and a place where the fifth should have been with nobody crossing himself and the boy keeping the heard bell and the told bell on two places, while at the Slate Row fringe a man whose name was on no roll with soft hands and a patient face handed a figure to a slate at the Court's table, holding it where nobody else could see and resting his thumb on the corner afterward without passing it over the number as Berr had, and the boy filed the soft hands apart from Marra, the Drawing collector, the Court-table clerk and the Fishstairs clerk, apart from the child and the loaf, and did not call it a sale, the soft-cuffed clerk still at the landing with hand to slate before eyes to stalls and no sixth sighting of the neat dark hand, and the boy lay ninety-nine days old inside an account that had gone over him twice without once addressing him or knowing his number, as at dusk the fire's payer went unnamed for ninety-nine days and one crust kept its unnamed empty place with no third.
Day 100 | Seed 11, Y.H. 813 (Firstday) | the Clay Yard, the barley fields east of Low Kiln and the bed under the Vail kiln-house roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | The boy was one hundred days old, three months and ten days, and nobody marked it, said it or gave him a figure for it, the seed standing in the strips where the fists had let it out and the yard going around the boot-print, the clean dark line, the new finer grey called thaw and the space under the lowest rack with a broom and a glance and no figure spoken, Sella giving the broom its instruction before anybody and never to the basket, Tarn's knife lying on its sill with six years standing in a mark his thumb had worn almost flat and the seventh nearly gone and still held while he said *Six counted. The next I don't count*, said *Yes, house* to an early and a late thaw and kept wanting the late because it puts off the paying, something having to give at the end of the seventh year that did not give on the hundredth morning, Jorra heard at the wheel and not seen with the back room unmentioned and *he's not Vail* sealed, and under the roof the private file checked unchanged with six hearings staying six beside and never among and no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and not paid, three intervals on another tray, the word forty unspoken with the readable double turn beside it and the weight of a thumb apart, four low things in four places with the river's note a fifth and not a hearing, the two tellings of the shut room joined to no kiln and no third telling, the damper's double bite filed as an object and the loan that can hear still uncalled, while the loaf shelf kept its two unnamed gaps and the fold its one stiff crust and one unnamed empty place in two rooms that did not touch and no third crust came, every warmth having a payer and none entered, and at dusk Sella set him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, put the fold right without looking at his face and left the thread frozen, the river's note coming through the finger's-width-open door and the fire's four, four and a gap through the floor in two separate places as for a hundred days, his hand going up an inch toward the note of water going over water and coming down with the count standing at one hundred, unspent.
Day 101 | Seed 12, Y.H. 813 (Secondday) | the Clay Yard, the loaf shelf in the Vail kiln-house and the bed under the Vail roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | The boy was one hundred and one days old and nobody said so, while a neighbour at the loaf shelf reached past the bare board and named the old space at the row's end as a thing that came in with the planting and the empty place at his ear as a child's appetite in one breath without once seeing they were one absence, a witness planted for a far-off account (T097), and Sella Vail said the house where another would say I, instructed the pot, fire and broom but never the basket, and left both gaps unfigured, while Tarn swept the collector's road over and over without once turning along it, his knife holding six counted years and a seventh nearly gone and still held as he told the kindling Six counted. It cares if they're steady*), telling a pot *You'll do* and putting that finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella's unfinished sentence so the household straightened around his silence, the iron taking the cold out of the fingertip and giving it back a little warmer, while Tarn took the broom only after it was instructed and his stroke checked half a beat behind Jorra's standing finger before going on without a word or a turn of the head, the two silences standing in one room with no hand joining them and the loan uncalled, at the well Sella sending the woman with wet sleeves to ask the pot what a wet thing costs because *the house has said it*, Berr Clay wiping his thumb twice on his apron, reading one in twelve and saying a number goes into a slate, not into a strip, then going off up the clay road with the box locked and the true subtraction inside believing he had done a kindness, a man putting his fist back in his sleeve so the figure arrived nowhere, Tarn saying *Yes, house* to an early thaw and a late while wanting the late because it puts off the paying, his chest tight and his breath unspent, and at going of light the count standing at one hundred and eleven, exact and unspent.
Day 112 | Seed 23, Y.H. 813 (Thirdday) | the Fishstairs below the north bridge and the outer boards of the fish-trade shade, House Silt three doors down, the loaf shelf in the Vail kiln-house and the bed under the Vail roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | Sella set the basket at the end of the shade where no slate lay, gave the instruction to the wool and the running water and never to the basket, and stood a half-pace from every open slate, while Mira Silt answered whether the run would be thin with her own answer (*Thin? Who's to say thin? It comes when it comes. Ask the river*), moved eel-bones against her thumb while deciding and put it under her apron to the grey cord when a buyer named a figure, shifting a creel to show the second cord twisted twice beneath it, neither knot counted, her board beside Orra Weir's knot-string and not touching it, the soft-cuffed clerk still set at the out-of-line landing with his slate for a measure nobody called and no sixth sighting, no foundling turning late and no loaf passing, and at midday three doors down Alda Reed laid her birth-slates on the bench before turning to the fold, pressed the wool a breath too long, crossed two fingers at the birth-flower before she knew it and covered the sign with a dead woman's date, said *Warm and breathing* which was exact and not true, went on with dates after the question stopped, touched the tin in her bodice without opening it and left her sixth slate face-down with six pages unread and no seventh while the pewter tin above the board-bed kept its pale fold and the grey wool below only the hollow of the pale stone, nobody saying either was gone, and under the roof at going of light the boy added what the day gave without entering any of it, the file unchanged, one crust stiff in the fold, the shelf's two gaps in the room that did not touch it, the cold foot still the cold, the widow's mark untouched, the carried fire missing its fifth breath with its payer unnamed for a hundred and twelve days, the river's note through the gap and the kiln's breath through the floor in two places that did not meet, his hand going up an inch toward the water and coming down as the count stood at one hundred and twelve, exact, unspent and spoken by nobody.
Day 113 | Seed 24, Y.H. 813 (Fourthday) | the worked strips east of Low Kiln, the loaf shelf and yard well in the Vail kiln-house, and the bed under the Vail roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | The last tend held with the seed up and the hands counted in glances and handfuls and never a figure, a man brought a number up out of a fist toward the well, looked at it and put it back in his sleeve so it arrived nowhere, Sella gave the bucket, broom, pot and fire their instructions before anybody and never the basket and sent a woman with wet sleeves to ask the pot what a wet thing costs because *the house has said it*, another neighbour at the loaf shelf reached past a bare board and in one breath laid the old gap at the row's end and the empty place at the boy's ear under one cause without seeing what she had done, the boy set her saying beside the shelf's two gaps and the fold's crust and its empty place on three places that did not touch, and at going of light the file was unchanged and one hundred and thirteen stood unspent, spoken by nobody.
Day 114 | Seed 25, Y.H. 813 (Fifthday) | the Vail wheel-shed and its finger's-width-open back room (not entered), the damper, the flagstones, House Silt three doors down and the bed under the Vail roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | Men came up before first grey and spoke low in the back room and Jorra gave them no name, came through with fine grey slate dust worked into both forearms past the bent finger, spoke to the wheel before anyone and told a pot it would do, and put that finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella's unfinished sentence so the household straightened around his silence, and this time Tarn's stroke went on over the flagstones without the half-check while the stones kept the place where it had stopped, neither man naming the other's silence and the loan uncalled, while three doors down Alda laid her birth-slates before the fold, crossed two fingers at the birth-flower before she knew it, covered the sign with a dead woman's date, said warm and breathing which was exact and not true, and left her sixth page unwritten with the pewter tin and the little tin shut, and at going of light one hundred and fourteen stood unspent.
Day 115 | Seed 26, Y.H. 813 (Sixthday) | the fish-trade shade below the north bridge, the out-of-line landing at the Fishstairs, the Cross and the bed under the Vail roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | Sella set the basket where no slate lay and gave the instruction to the wool and the running water and never to the basket, Mira answered whether the run would be thin with her own answer and put her thumb under her apron to the grey cord when a buyer named a figure, a shift of a creel showing the second cord twisted twice beneath it with neither knot counted and her board beside Orra's not touching, the soft-cuffed clerk stayed set at the landing for a measure nobody called, at the Cross a soft-handed man from Slate Row handed a figure to a slate held at the edge where nobody else could see it and rested his thumb on the corner with no sixth sighting and no sale, and at going of light the boy turned out his unchanged file, added the day's six objects without entering any of them, and held one hundred and fifteen exact and unspent as his hand went up an inch toward the water and came down.
Day 116 | Seed 27, Y.H. 813 (Seventhday) | the worked strips east of Low Kiln, the loaf shelf in the Vail kiln-house and the bed under the roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | The last hands came out of the worked strips with the seed up, counted in glances and handfuls and never a figure --- two fingers lifted with chaff in their creases, a barrow-man shaping a number with his mouth and thinking better of it --- and one hand that had gone in on Seed 15 did not come out with the rest, so the yard went around the empty place in the line with a look and no number, T098 planted with no name, no cause, no body and no payment, while Sella Vail carried the boy at the edge of the work at her half-pace from every open slate, gave the instruction to the wool and the river wind and never to the basket and said the house where another woman would have said I, the boy reading the going-around as a chart closed with a neat line over a note nobody had opened and setting the field's empty place on a place of its own, and at the loaf shelf a neighbour reached past the bare board and called the old gap a planting and the new palm's breadth the price of a wet thing set down wrong without seeing she had joined two rooms, while Sella glanced once at the clay jar and did not touch the widow's mark, and at the going of the light the boy found his file unchanged, added the day's two objects on places of their own and held one hundred and sixteen unspent.
Day 117 | Seed 28, Y.H. 813 (Eighthday) | the Vail wheel-shed and the finger's-width-open back room (not entered), the damper, the flagstones, the stalls beyond the Cross and the bed under the Vail roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | Before first grey men came up the Clay Yard with their collars high and spoke low in the back room and Jorra Vail gave them no name and did not say the room was cold, coming through with fine grey slate dust ground into both forearms past the bent finger, not bone-coloured slip, keeping dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray and asking neither which slate was broken nor whether it was a birth-slate, speaking to the wheel before anyone and telling a pot it would do and withholding its full note from a High Kiln kiln-master, and putting that finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella's unfinished sentence so the household straightened around his silence while the boy read one piece of iron as the bite that holds a vessel whole and the bite that takes a hand off a man with no Grathic word for both, and Tarn took the broom only after it had been instructed, his seventh year pressed to the sill and still held, the breath from Seed 16 unspent with a small interval at the top of each reach, his stroke going on over the flagstones without the half-check while the stones kept the shallow bright patch where it had stopped and neither man named the other's silence and the loan stayed uncalled, while across the market a silent woman with lead-glaze green at one corner of her mouth stood looking at pots and the boy filed the colour beside two other greens without a name, a number going from a fist to a mouth to a shoulder and arriving nowhere, and at the going of the light one hundred and seventeen stood unspent with he's not Vail sealed and the promise of the foundling's name neither given nor withdrawn.
Day 118 | Seed 29, Y.H. 813 (Ninthday) | the yard well, the loaf shelf in the Vail kiln-house, the Fishstairs below the north bridge, House Silt three doors down and the bed under the Vail roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | A neighbour come up from the strips asked what the planting cost now the hands were out of it and Sella glanced at the clay jar and sent her to the pot with Ask the pot what a wet thing costs set down there, the house has said it, so the answer went off unanswered, and at the loaf shelf a second neighbour reached for the bare board before her eyes found the boy and said in one breath that the old gap came in with the planting and the empty place at his ear was a child's appetite, laying two rooms under one cause without seeing it, which the boy filed beside the Seed 24 saying and the earlier tellings on two places with no joining made his own, T097 advanced and not paid with no third gap and no fourth likeness, while at dawn Mira Silt answered whether the run would be thin with her own answer and put her thumb under her apron to the grey cord when a buyer named a figure, showing the second cord twisted twice beneath it with neither knot counted and her board beside Orra Weir's and not touching, and three doors down Alda Reed laid her birth-slates before the fold, crossed two fingers at the birth-flower before she knew it, covered the sign with a dead woman's date, said Warm and breathing which was exact and not true, and left her sixth narrow slate turned down with no seventh, the pewter tin and the little tin shut, while below the sill a child's foot stayed dark in three turns of wool and at the going of the light one hundred and eighteen stood unspent.
Day 119 | Seed 30, Y.H. 813 (Tenthday, Account-day and the last market of Seed) | the Cross reading block and moot-post's shade, the worked strips east of Low Kiln, the Fishstairs out-of-line landing and the bed under the Vail roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | The planting month ended and Reed came on with one place in the returning line still gone around with a look and no figure, T098 carried and unpaid, while Berr Clay came up to the block short with the red cord of his office folded under his coat and green at one mouth-corner, wiped his thumb twice before touching nothing, held a narrow slate unopened to his forearm, read one in twelve as the notice says, called the levy and said it was not called by him, and told the man who brought a number up out of a fist that a number goes into a slate not into a strip and your house never I, taking himself out of his own sentence so that the figure read was not the figure paid and did not know the hand that had not come back, while the bell went four four and a gap and nobody crossed himself, the soft-cuffed clerk stayed set at the out-of-line landing for a measure nobody called and the market walked over the missing step carefully without making a fall of it, and under the roof at the going of the light the boy found his file unchanged with six hearings and no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and not paid, the word forty unspoken, one crust and two shelf gaps in rooms that did not touch, the held breath unspent and the loan uncalled, added the day's objects on places of their own, and held one hundred and nineteen exact and unspent as his hand went up an inch toward the water and came down with nothing joined, named, paid or ended.
Day 120 | Reed 1, Y.H. 813 (Firstday) | the yard at Low Kiln, the edge of the worked strips east of it, the Vail kiln-house loaf shelf and the bed under the Vail roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | Reed came on without a boundary drawn as the wind off the Ilm brought wet mud and cut grass downriver and the yard turned toward the reeds, the work spoken of as a direction and a going-downriver and never as a figure with a bundle judged by the arm that carried it, while a woman come up from the strips asked what the reeds would cost now the hands were out of them and Sella Vail glanced once at the clay jar and sent her to the pot with Ask the pot what a wet thing costs set down there, the house has said it, and the yard went around the clean dark line, the new finer grey called the thaw, the space beneath the lowest rack where the broken birth-slates lay entered by nobody and the place in the worked strip where a hand had gone in with the seed and had not come out with the rest, with a look and a wide step and no number (T098 carried, not paid), and under the roof Sella instructed the bucket, broom, pot and fire before anybody and never the basket, moved her lips along the loaf row without a figure, set the boy, one hundred and twenty days old, on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, put the fold right without looking at his face, left the thread frozen and unwiped, told the fire it was the thaw, turned the coals with the back of a broken pot and said The house will keep it, while he read the field's going-around as a chart closed over an unopened note, exact, complete and worth nothing, and kept six hearings with no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and not paid, the told bell beside the heard bell and the word forty unspoken as the river's note came through the finger's-width gap and the fire's four, four and a gap came through the floor in two places that did not meet.

Orra Weir pulled one knot down with her thumb and gave a date --- *The ninth of Ilmen*, the collector's boat with six oars and one man at the stern who never touched them --- where a figure was asked, saying the river takes what the Court does not, her knot-string lying beside Mira's board and not touching it with the forty-first double turn legible and the word forty unspoken, while Mira answered a thin run with *Ask the river*, moved eel-bones while deciding whether to lie and kept her thumb under her apron to the grey cord longer than the figure required, a shifting creel showing the second twist twisted twice that was never carried to Nine Pots or lifted at a door, neither knot counted and the thin child's knot untouched, and did not look into the basket; at dusk Sella set him on his bed under the roof, told the fire it was the thaw and went to her own bed, and he, one hundred and twenty-eight days old and told by nobody, found every object in the file in its place with the second stopping on the interval tray, six hearings and no seventh, three answers unpaid, the word forty unspoken and the cold foot still the cold, as the river's note came through the finger's-width gap, the fire missed its fifth breath with its payer unnamed for a hundred and twenty-eight days and the boards kept a knot the width of a thumb, three counts in three places that did not become one, his hand going up an inch toward the water and coming down with the count unspent.
Day 129 | Reed 10, Y.H. 813 (Tenthday, the first Account-day of Reed) | the Cross reading block and the moot-post's shade, the stalls beyond, the out-of-line landing below the north bridge, the Vail kiln-house loaf shelf and hearth, the clay road and the bed under the Vail roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | On the first Account-day of Reed Sella Vail carried the boy at the half-pace into the moot-post's shade where no slate lay and stood a half-pace off while two hundred leaned over the block and eight pigs went over it with an assessor's hand on the slate before his eyes went to the rail; Berr Clay came up short with his office cord folded under his coat and green glaze at one mouth-corner, wiped his thumb twice before touching nothing, passed a finger over his narrow slate, read *one in twelve, as the notice says*, called the levy and said it was not called by him, and to the man who brought a number up out of a fist said there would be a slate at the watch --- *your house*, never *I* --- so the figure went into the air while the true subtraction stayed in the locked box up the clay road; the bell went four, four and a gap with nobody crossing himself and the heard bell was kept beside the told bell, the soft-cuffed clerk stayed set below the bridge for a measure nobody called with hand to slate before eyes to stalls and the market sold over him, and a man from the strips went around the place in the returning line where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out on Seed 27 with a look and no number (T098 carried, not paid); back under the Vail roof at midday Sella set the basket low near the bench leg at the angle where the underside of the loaf shelf becomes a roof, and from that angle the boy first saw the short charcoal marks in clusters on the board's underside, some pressed hard, some faded nearly into the grain, a keeping put where nobody thought to look, which he did not read, count, copy or lay beside the two gaps above, the crust in the fold or any other private record but set on a place of its own, advanced and unpaid (T100 planted), while a neighbour who asked what the row would want before the tend was out was sent to the pot with *the house has said it* and carried the unanswered thing away level; at dusk Sella carried him up the clay road, went around the rack space, set him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, put the fold right without looking at his face, left the thread frozen, told the fire it was the thaw and said *The house will keep it*, and the river's note, the fire's silent fifth and the boards' knot were three counts in three places that did not become one as one hundred and twenty-nine stood exact, unspent and spoken by nobody.
Day 130 | Reed 11, Y.H. 813 (Firstday) | the Clay Yard, the Vail wheel-shed and its finger's-width-open back room (not entered), the damper, the flagstones, the fish-trade shade and out-of-line landing at the Fishstairs, below the sill, the hearth and kindling under the Vail roof and the bed under the roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | Before first grey three or four unnamed men came up the Clay Yard with their collars high and spoke low in the back room, which kept its finger's width of open, and Jorra Vail gave them no name and did not say the room was cold, coming through with fine grey slate dust ground small as meal into both forearms past the bent little finger, not bone-coloured slip, keeping dusty and clean forearms on one tray and asking neither which slate had been broken nor whether it was a birth-slate; he spoke to the wheel before anyone (*It doesn't care whose hands. It cares if they're steady*), told a pot *You'll do*, knew its full note before it left the wheel and withheld it from a High Kiln kiln-master who would call it early, and put his bent finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella's unfinished sentence so the household straightened around his silence, while the boy read one piece of iron as the bite that holds a vessel whole and the bite that takes a hand off a man with no Grathic word for both and filed it as an object joined to no kiln, and no third telling of the shut counting room came; Tarn took the broom only after it had been instructed, said *Yes, house* to an early thaw and a late while wanting the late because it puts off the paying, his seventh year pressed past another tend with six years in a worn thumb-mark and the seventh nearly gone, and his stroke went on over the flagstones without the half-check while the stones kept the shallow bright patch and neither man named the other's silence and the loan stayed uncalled; in the afternoon at the Fishstairs the soft-cuffed clerk was still set for a measure nobody called and entered a buyer's figure before his eyes found the man who had spoken it, while below the sill a woman wound a child's dark foot in three turns of wool and called it the cold and a neighbour at the tubs called the water weather, the boy reading the extremity going before the core and the afterdrop waiting on a warming nobody would perform and buying nothing with it; at the hearth, coals banked and the small knife set back where it could be checked, Tarn told the kindling *Six counted. The next I don't count* and the sentence about an ear worth more than the debt came a third time to the word that would call the loan and stopped with no figure and no name, so he drew the breath and did not spend it, said *Yes, house* to the fire and went on with the broom, Sella within hearing asking nothing and Jorra not asking about the ear while Tarn did not ask about the room, and the boy laid the third stopping on the interval tray beside the first two as an object and not a third payment or a doctrine, with the loan uncalled, the seventh year not given and one hundred and thirty exact and unspent as the carried fire missed its fifth breath with its payer unnamed for a hundred and thirty days.
Day 131 | Reed 12, Y.H. 813 (Secondday) | the river road downriver, the Weir plank walk, the flat blessing stone and lower boards, House Silt three doors down, the Vail kiln-house loaf shelf and hearth, the clay road and the bed under the Vail roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | Sella carried the boy downriver at the half-pace to the Weir, where salt stood white on the posts and the traps had their mouths upriver, and the reed work went on in armfuls judged by the carrying arm and by nothing set on a slate, a cutter telling a girl with a creel *Lift it. Your arm'll tell you. It'll tell you what went into it, and that's the whole of what it knows*; the reed-cutter came along the boards with a bundle and the grey cord inside his coat gone grey with the oil of a working thumb, set the bundle on the blessing stone, straightened the cord, turned it so the knots stood, tied one low with his teeth and a pull of the thumb, bit the end off and put it back inside his coat, saying *You can ask the cord* and *No more can the Court* with no figure, knot, name or joining (T099 carried, not paid), while Orra Weir at the lower boards pulled a knot down and gave a date --- the ninth of Ilmen, the collector's boat with six oars and the man at the stern who never touched them --- saying *It's a date. The river takes what the Court doesn't* with the forty-first double turn legible and the word forty unspoken, and Mira Silt worked the eels with slime dried grey on her sleeves and silt pale in her neck's hollow, answered a thin run with her own answer, moved eel-bones while deciding whether to lie and put her thumb under her apron to the grey cord when a buyer named a figure, the second twist twisted twice beneath it never carried to Nine Pots or lifted at a door, neither knot counted, the thin child's knot untouched and her board lying beside Orra's without touching; at midday Sella set the basket just inside the finger's-width-open door of House Silt and stood a half-pace off, and Alda Reed laid her birth-slates before turning to the fold, pressed the wool a breath too long, crossed two fingers at the red edge of the birth-flower unknowing, covered the sign with the date she gave Dessa, said *Warm and breathing, that's all I've set down* (exact and not true over a woman more mornings dead than any living person keeps count of), touched the tin in her bodice without opening it and left six pages turned toward a floorboard with no seventh while the pewter tin above the abandoned bed kept its pale fold and thumb-bright rub shut; in the afternoon back under the Vail roof Sella reached a finger beneath the loaf shelf where the charcoal tally lay, without looking at it and without a word, and brought it away, and the boy saw the hand go under and come back and made no cause of it (T100 carried, not paid), and at dusk she carried him up, went around the rack space, set him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, put the fold right, left the thread frozen, told the fire it was the thaw and counted under her breath toward no opening, the river's note, the fire's silent fifth with its payer unnamed for a hundred and thirty-one days and the boards' four nails, four, and a knot the width of a thumb standing as three counts in three places that did not become one, his hand going up an inch toward the water and coming down with one hundred and thirty-one exact, unspent and spoken by nobody.
Day 132 | Reed 13, Y.H. 813 (Thirdday) | the Clay Yard, the drying racks and the edge of the worked strips, the Vail kiln-house loaf shelf and hearth, the Weir plank walk, the flat blessing stone and lower boards, the fish-trade shade and the bed under the Vail roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | The reed month stood in its middle tend as Sella Vail carried the boy, one hundred and thirty-two days old and four months and twelve days, at the half-pace from every open slate, giving the instruction to the wool and the river wind and never to the basket, going around the clean dark line, the new finer grey called the thaw, the space under the lowest rack where the broken birth-slates lay and the place in the returning line where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, with a look and a wide step and no number (T098 carried, not paid), while reeds came in armfuls judged by the arm that carried them, a cutter telling a girl with a creel that her arm knew what went into the bundle and that was the whole of it, and a man who asked what the work would want before the tend was out being given the weather and the river; Day 140 | Reed 21, Y.H. 813 (Firstday) | the Vail wheel-shed and its finger's-width-open back room (not entered), the damper, the flagstones and the Clay Yard, the Weir plank walk, flat blessing stone and lower boards, the fish-trade shade below the sill, the Vail kiln-house loaf shelf, bed and hearth, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | Before first grey three or four men with their collars high went low-voiced into the room off the shed whose door kept its finger's width of open, and Sella Vail carried the boy past at the half-pace and gave the house no name for them and did not say the room was cold, while Jorra Vail came through with fine grey slate dust ground small as meal into both forearms past the bent little finger, keeping dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray, speaking to the wheel before anyone, telling a pot You'll do and withholding its full note from a High Kiln kiln-master who said it was singing before its time, and putting that bent finger into the cold iron of the damper ahead of Sella's unfinished sentence so the household straightened around his silence, the boy filing one piece of iron with two bites as an object joined to no kiln with no third telling of the shut room (T062, T065/T095); Tarn's seventh year pressed nearer its end and still held, his stroke going on over the flagstones past the bright patch without the half-check, the unforged collector sentence and the Seed 16 breath unspent beside the knife at the edge of its sill; downriver at the Weir a reed-cutter straightened his grey thumb-oiled cord on the flat blessing stone, turned it once so the knots stood, tied one low with his teeth and bit the end off and put it back inside his coat, telling a woman who could not read it You can ask the cord and No more can the Court (T099 carried, not paid), while Orra Weir pulled one knot down and gave the ninth of Ilmen, the collector's boat with six oars and one man at the stern who never touched them, with the forty-first double turn legible and the word forty unspoken, and Mira Silt answered a thin run with her own answer, moved eel-bones while deciding whether to lie and kept her thumb under her apron to a grey cord with a second twist twisted twice beneath it never carried upriver to Nine Pots or lifted at a door, neither knot counted (T024/T059/T025), and below the sill the child's foot stayed dark in three turns of wool; in the small hours Sella set him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft with the fold right and the thread frozen unwiped, told the fire it was the thaw and said The house will keep it, and he turned out his file and found every object in its place and nothing laid across anything else --- six hearings of the full note beside and never among with no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and not paid, six stoppings of the near-saying as objects and not a rule, the damper's double bite, the two shut-room tellings with no third, the heard bell beside the told, the fifth green a colour and not a name, the word forty unspoken, the cold foot worth nothing, one crust in the fold and two shelf gaps in rooms that did not touch, every private keeping unread --- and one hundred and forty days old, four months and twenty days, wanted the crust two inches from his ear and the number spoken by somebody who would know what it counted, and got neither, his hand going up an inch toward the note of water over water and coming down against the fold, exact, complete and unspent.
Day 141 | Reed 22, Y.H. 813 (Secondday) | the Clay Yard, the drying racks and reed beds below Low Kiln, the Vail kiln-house loaf shelf and hearth, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | The reed month went into its last week without a boundary drawn as Sella Vail carried the boy, one hundred and forty-one days old and four months and twenty-one days, at the half-pace from every open slate, instruction to the wool and the river wind and never the basket, while the last bundles came up judged by the arm that carried them, a cutter telling a girl with a creel that her arm knew what went into a bundle and that was the whole of it, and a woman who asked what the hands would be paid being answered with the weather and the river and shutting two fingers out of a fist; the yard went around the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the broken birth-slates under the lowest rack and the place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, with a look and a wide step and no number (T098 carried), and a reed-cutter's grey cord went past along the boards straightened and turned where no slate lay with its knots unread (T099 carried); under the roof a neighbour reached past the bare board with her hand before her eyes and named the old shelf-gap and the empty place at the boy's ear under one appetite in one breath, a further shaping of T097 filed on a place of its own, advanced and not paid, no third gap and no cause made, while Sella moved her lips along the row, glanced once at the clay jar cold under its glaze, sent the woman to the pot with the house has said it and reached a finger beneath the board where the charcoal tally lay without looking or a word, and brought it away (T100 carried, unread), the widow's mark untouched because a shelf and an afternoon are not openings, and the boy read the carrying arm as a record in muscle that tells what was carried and not what it cost, exact, complete and worth nothing, one hundred and forty-one going on with nobody's thumb upon it.
Day 142 | Reed 23, Y.H. 813 (Thirdday) | the Vail wheel-shed and its finger's-width-open back room (not entered), the damper, the flagstones, the Cross and market stalls, the out-of-line landing below the north bridge, the hearth and kindling under the Vail roof and the bed under the roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | Before first grey three or four men with collars high went low-voiced into the room off the shed and Sella Vail carried the boy past at the half-pace, giving them no name and not saying the room was cold, while Jorra Vail came through with grey slate dust ground small as meal into both forearms past the bent finger, spoke to the wheel before anyone, told a pot You'll do, knew its full note and withheld it from a High Kiln kiln-master who said it was singing before its time, and put his bent finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella's unfinished sentence so the household straightened around his silence, the boy filing one iron with two bites as an object joined to no kiln with no third telling of the shut room (T062, T065/T095); Tarn's seventh year pressed nearer its end than ever and still held, his stroke going on over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without the half-check; at the Cross Berr Clay read one in twelve, called the levy and denied it with your house, never I, paid two marks short for two pair of eels which the stall-keeper put in her palm without counting where anyone could hear, and went up the road with the true subtraction locked in the box believing he had done a kindness, while below the bridge the soft-cuffed clerk stayed set for a measure nobody called; under the roof at the going of the light Tarn told the kindling Six counted. The next I don't count and brought the ear-sentence a SEVENTH time --- on Reed 23 after Reed 5, 8, 11, 14, 17 and 20 --- all the way to the word that would call the loan, stopping there with no figure and no name and drawing the breath he did not spend, and the boy filed the seventh stopping on the interval tray beside the six as an interval and not a seventh payment, refusing to let seven likenesses stand up and call themselves a doctrine because no payer had been named to any, the loan uncalled, the seventh year one tend from its end and the fire's payer unnamed for a hundred and forty-two days, one hundred and forty-two standing exact and unspent.

Orra Weir pulled one knot down and gave the ninth of Ilmen, the collector's boat with six oars and the man at the stern who never touched them, keeping the forty-first double turn legible and the word forty unspoken, while Mira Silt answered a thin run with Ask the river, flicked eel-bones while deciding whether to lie, and when a buyer named a figure put her thumb under her apron to the grey cord with a second twist twisted twice beneath it, never carried upriver to Nine Pots or lifted at a door, neither knot counted, her board beside Orra's and not touching (T024/T059/T025), so that three private records stood within a dozen paces of the basket, visible and none enterable, and below the sill a child's foot stayed dark in three turns of wool, the cold to the woman who wrapped it and weather to the yard, the boy's reading of the extremity going before the core and the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody would perform exact and worth nothing with no silt-leach, cause or cure named (T093/T094/T096); the soft-cuffed clerk stayed set at the landing for the uncalled measure, and in the afternoon the last bundles stood grey in the ruts with nobody counting them, the third Account-day six days off, while the yard went around the clean dark line, the thaw, the broken birth-slates and the place where the hand had gone in on Seed 15 and not come out, with a look and a wide step and no number (T098 carried); under the roof a neighbour with a wet pot was sent to the pot with the house has said it and Sella, moving her lips along the row with its two unnamed gaps, reached a finger beneath the board where the charcoal lay without looking or a word (T100 carried, unread), the two rooms not touching, and at going of light she carried him up around the pan and iced trough, set him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, put the fold right without looking at his face, left the thread frozen, told the fire it was the thaw and said The house will keep it, and in the small hours he turned out his file and found it exact, complete and worth nothing with seven stoppings on the tray and no payer named to any, one hundred and forty-three unspent and the loan uncalled with the seventh year one tend from its end.
Day 144 | Reed 25, Y.H. 813 (Fifthday) | the Clay Yard, the drying racks and reed beds below Low Kiln, the Vail kiln-house loaf shelf and hearth, the bed under the Vail roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | The reed month went out without a boundary drawn as Sella Vail carried the boy, one hundred and forty-four days old and four months and twenty-four days, at the half-pace from every open slate, instruction to the wool and the river wind and never the basket, while the last bundles came up in armfuls judged by the arm that carried them, a cutter telling a girl with a creel that her arm knew what went into a bundle and that was the whole of what it knew, and a man who asked what the hands would be paid being answered with the weather and the river, never a figure (T071/T072, T077); the yard went around the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the space beneath the lowest rack where the broken birth-slates lay and the empty place in the returning line where a hand went in on Seed 15 and had not come out, with a look and a wide step and no number (T098 carried), and a reed-cutter's grey cord went past along the boards straightened and turned where no slate lay with its knots unread (T099 carried); under the roof Sella set the basket low near the bench leg at the angle where the board's underside becomes a roof, moved her lips along the row with its two unnamed gaps, glanced once at the clay jar cold under its glaze and reached a finger BENEATH the board where the charcoal tally lay without looking and without a word, brought it away and did not go back to the shelf (T100 carried, unread), told the fire it was the thaw, turned the coals with the back of a broken pot, said The house will keep it, counted under her breath toward no opening, pushed coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist and left the widow's mark untouched, while the boy read the carrying arm as a record in muscle that tells what was carried and not what it cost, exact, complete and worth nothing, held seven stoppings on the interval tray with no payer named to any and refused to bring the eighth early into the yard to make a row come out even, and one hundred and forty-four went on exact and unspent with nobody's thumb upon it.

Day 146 | Reed 27, Y.H. 813 (Seventhday) | House Silt three doors down, the finger's-width-open door, the plank walk and lower boards at the Weir, the fish-trade shade, the clay road, the pan set out to dry and the iced trough by the well, the Vail kiln-house loaf shelf, hearth and bed under the roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | Sella Vail set the basket just inside the finger's-width-open door of House Silt at the edge of the light and stood a half-pace off, asking nothing about the writing, the tin, the sign or the date, while Alda Reed came short with soap-and-milk gone cold under river silt and lye sour under the soap, laid her birth-slates writing-down on the bench before turning to the fold, pressed the wool flat at his shoulder a breath longer than a fold requires, touched the little tin in her bodice without opening it, crossed two fingers at the red edge of the birth-flower before she knew she had done it and covered the sign with the date she had given Dessa, Stone seven. The account went up on the eighth, before the paper went out, standing over a woman more mornings dead than any living person keeps count of and uncollected; to He lies quiet she said Warm and breathing, that's all I've set down, exact and not true, and went on with the cooper's seventh in Mud End, a potter's third child in Stonemouth and the last high water after the question had stopped, leaving six pages in a second hand turned face-down toward a floorboard in a house the boy could not name, no seventh written, the round pewter tin above the abandoned board-bed shut with its pale fold and thumb-bright rub, the grey wool below holding only the hollow where the small pale river stone had lain, nobody saying either was gone (T007/T008, T023/T089), while the boy, who could not read Grathic, kept sign, turned slate and covered flower on places of their own and made no cause (T061/T082); in the small hours he turned out his file as a man lays instruments on a towel --- six hearings of the full note with no seventh, the four near-full answers advanced and not paid, the older intervals with the unchecking stroke beside the half-beat, EIGHT stoppings on the widened interval tray (Reed 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20, 23 and 26) as objects and not a rule with no payer named to any, the damper's two bites joined to no kiln, the two shut-room tellings with no third, the told bell beside the heard bell --- while the charcoal under the shelf waited for a hand that was not his, the fifth green stayed a colour joined to no ear, the word forty stayed unspoken, the soft-cuffed clerk stayed set for the uncalled measure and the cold foot stayed the cold below the sill, and three counts in three places --- the river's note unnumbered, the fire's missing fifth pull and the fifth that was a knot and not a nail --- did not become one, so that one hundred and forty-six stood exact and unspent and spoken by nobody as his hand went up an inch toward the note of water over water and came down against the fold, the loan uncalled and the seventh year one tend from its end.

toward the note of water over water and came down against the fold, the reed month going out without a boundary drawn and the count crossing into Smoke with the loan uncalled and the seventh year one tend from its end.
Day 150 | Tallow 1, Y.H. 813 (Firstday) | the Clay Yard and the kiln mouth, the drying racks and the edge of the worked strips, the yard well, the Vail wheel-shed and its finger's-width-open back room (not entered), the damper and the flagstones, the Vail kiln-house hearth and the bed under the roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | The firing month opened at last as Sella Vail carried the boy, one hundred and fifty days old and five months exactly and told by nobody, at the half-pace from every open slate with instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot and the broom and never to the basket, and at the kiln mouth she put her hand to the widow's mark before the opening, held it one breath, let go and did not touch it again, tipping the coal under the back of a broken pot while the fire answered four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been with its payer unnamed for a hundred and fifty days (T058/T079, T088, T071/T072); the kilns had been brought up for the year's last working season and the danger changed address to the kiln's breath in fours with a gap, hot clay, grey slate dust ground small as meal under the nails and the sweetish edge of lead glaze on a wrong wind off High Kiln, a yard woman speaking sideways of a man in Mud End taken in his sleep and nobody making a lesson of it, while the trough by the well had lost its skin of ice and was called weather, the clay jar stood cold under its glaze and the pan set out to dry through Reed was gone from its place with no scrape, crumb, print or word and nobody saying so (T062, T097); the yard went around the clean dark line where the Ash ridge had turned, the finer grey called the thaw, the broken birth-slates under the lowest rack and the place in the returning line where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried), and before first grey three or four unnamed men had gone low-voiced into the finger's-width-open back room with no name given and no third telling of the counting room (T035/T031, T065/T095); Jorra Vail came through with fine grey slate dust ground small as meal into both forearms past the bent little finger, spoke to the wheel before anyone, told a pot You'll do, knew its full note and withheld it from a High Kiln kiln-master who said it was singing before its time, and put that bent finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella's unfinished sentence so the household straightened around his silence, the boy filing one iron with two bites joined to no kiln and the knowing among the near-full answers and not among the hearings (T062, T061/T082); Tarn took the broom only after it had been instructed, his seventh year one tend from its end and still held, the knife at the very edge of its sill with six counted where the house could check and the seventh where it could not, the unforged collector sentence beside it, the Seed 16 breath unspent with its small interval at the top of each reach, his chest tight since the dark and Ash worked into his knuckle creases, and his stroke went on over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without even the half-check while he did not turn along the collector road and no collector came, neither man naming the other's silence (T036/T076); at dusk she went wide around the pan's empty place, the ice-less trough and the rack space, set him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, put the fold right without looking at his face, left the thread frozen, rested her hand a half-beat longer, told the fire it was the thaw, said The house will keep it, counted under her breath toward no opening, set the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand and left the widow's mark untouched because a dusk is not an opening, and in the small hours his file held six hearings of the full note beside and never among with no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and not paid, the older intervals and NINE stoppings --- Reed 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20, 23, 26 and 29 --- as objects and not a rule with no payer named to any, the damper's double bite, the two shut-room tellings with no third and the told bell beside the heard bell, while three counts in three places --- the river's note unnumbered, the fire's missing fifth and the fifth that was a knot and not a nail --- did not become one, so that one hundred and fifty stood exact, complete and unspent as his hand went up an inch toward the note of water and came down against the fold.
Day 151 | Tallow 2, Y.H. 813 (Secondday) | the river road downriver, the Weir plank walk on posts, the flat blessing stone and lower boards, the fish-trade shade below the sill, the out-of-line landing below the north bridge, the clay road, the Vail kiln-house loaf shelf and hearth, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath | The last of the reed work went downriver as a direction rather than a bundle, counted in the arm that carried it, and Sella Vail set the basket at the edge of the work where no slate lay with instruction to the wool and the running water and never to the basket, while a woman who asked what the hands would be paid for the going down and the coming back was answered with the going down and the coming back and went off with the question still in her mouth and no entry anywhere (T071/T072, T077, T058/T079); the boy, one hundred and fifty-one days old and five months and a day, watched the reed-cutter set his bundle on the flat blessing stone, straighten his grey thumb-oiled cord, turn it once so the knots stood, tie one low with his teeth, bite the end off and put it back inside his coat with the flat of his hand, saying You can ask the cord and No more can the Court and going up the boards to lift a trap with no figure and no knot counted (T099 carried), while below the stone Orra Weir, her hands like old rope, the pale eel scars uncovered, salt white at her wrists, the grey streak first through the black hair and the Fen half-song flat in her voice, pulled one knot down and gave the ninth of Ilmen, the collector's boat round the bend on the flood with six oars and one man at the stern who never touched them, saying It's a date. The river takes what the Court doesn't. You can shout at either one. I've tried, and keeping the forty-first double turn legible with the word forty unspoken (T024/T059/T025); below the sill Mira Silt, pale eel slime dried in grey strokes on her sleeves and silt pale in the hollow of her neck, her head held a little right where the top of her left ear had been and her small smile kept like a door on the latch, answered a thin run with Thin? Who's to say thin? It comes when it comes. Ask the river, flicked eel-bones while deciding whether to lie, and when a buyer named a figure said Two marks the pair and two short. You've said it twice and I've counted it twice. There's nothing in the sentence that wants an answer, her thumb going under her apron to the grey cord and staying longer than the figure required with the second twist twisted twice beneath a shifting creel, never carried upriver to Nine Pots or lifted at a door, her board beside Orra's and not touching (T059/T025/T024); a child's foot below the shade stayed dark inside three turns of wool, the cold to the woman who wound it and weather to the neighbour with a pail, the boy's reading of the extremity going before the core, the almost-smile that is not peace and the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody would perform exact and worth nothing with no silt-leach, cause or cure named (T093/T094/T096 carried), while the soft-cuffed clerk stayed set at the out-of-line landing for an uncalled measure with his cuff grey from washing and grey again by midday, his slate inward and his hand to it before his eyes went to the stalls, and the market sold over him as water goes over a stone that lies where a stone lies (T090/T080 carried), five private records standing within a dozen paces of the basket and none enterable with no foundling, no loaf, no slate and no sale (T033/T034 held); under the roof in the going of the light the pan's gone place on the wall kept the exact width of a thing taken away with no dust disturbed and the boy held it on a tray of its own, apart from the shelf's two unnamed gaps, the stiff brown-edged crust two inches from his ear in the other room, the field's empty place and the sixth colour and sixth shape, with no third gap and no fourth likeness made a cause (T060/T086, T097 advanced, T098, T050/T051, T033/T034); the clay jar stood cold under its glaze and Sella glanced at it once and did not touch it, then stood with her back to the basket, moved her lips along the row with its two gaps and, without looking or a word, reached a finger BENEATH the front edge where the charcoal tally lies, held it a breath out and back, brought it away and did not go back to the shelf, such a hand either knowing the board by heart or told not to look with the reason standing between the two (T100 carried, unread); a neighbour with a wet pot who asked what a firing cost set down there was sent to the pot with Ask the pot what a wet thing costs set down there. The house has said it and carried the unanswered question away level so nothing slopped (T077), and at the hearth Sella told the fire it was the thaw, turned the coals with the back of a broken pot, said The house will keep it, counted under her breath toward no opening and left the widow's mark hanging where it hung because an afternoon is not an opening, while the fire gave four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been with its payer unnamed for a hundred and fifty-one days (T088, T058/T079), so that one hundred and fifty-one stood exact and unspent with the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand and the charcoal waiting under the shelf for a hand that was not his.
